newsitem.title: UK: British water firms improving service, some lag.
newsitem.headline: British water firms improving service, some lag.

text.p: British water companies improved service to customers overall in 1995-96 but some are still showing a deterioration, according to a report by industry regulator Ofwat published on Thursday.

In a statement to coincide with publication of "1995-96 Levels of Service" report, industry regulator Ofwat head Ian Byatt said "not all companies (have improved services) and the overall effect is a slower improvement than in past years."
He added that a long, dry summer in 1995 followed by a freeze and then thaw in early 1996 had meant more hosepipe bans and supply interruptions.
Ofwat's report said that payments made as compensation under the Guaranteed Standards Scheme (GSS) increased four-fold to 37,458 from a year ago.

Written complaints to companies rose by nearly 10 percent to 171,000 while unplanned disruptions lasting over 12 hours more than doubled to 130,206, as did the number of customers cut off for over 24 hours.
But Ofwat said quality of drinking water continued to improve with 99.5 percent of all water quality tests meeting required standards.
